messages:
maya: heads-up — Acme reported a billing delta for March usage. Their invoice shows 52,142 tokens for a single spike on 2026-02-28 but our SDK estimates and local logs only add up to ~48.9k. They attached a request id: req_0a9f3c and a sample conversation. Can billing look? :thinking:

jordan: thanks — do we have the raw request payload or the API response id? differences usually come from system messages or function outputs getting counted differently.

maya: pasted their minimal repro below (redacted keys). note they use the JS SDK v2.3.1 and say their client-side estimator uses tiktoken-lite.

mayanote: ```bash
# curl example they used (redacted)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-2.1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a concise assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the attached log and call get_weather() if needed."}],"functions":[{"name":"get_weather","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}}}}],"temperature":0.0}'
```

mayanote: API response (trimmed):
```json
{"id":"req_0a9f3c","object":"chat.completion","usage":{"prompt_tokens":22,"completion_tokens":94,"total_tokens":116},"choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":null,"function_call":{"name":"get_weather","arguments":"{\"city\":\"SF\"}"}} , {"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"It's sunny in SF..."}}]}
```

maya: their SDK estimator (client) returns ~101 total tokens for the same message set. they say the difference comes from the function_call arguments and the final assistant content being double-counted locally vs the API counts.

jordan: that snippet is useful. two likely causes: (1) server-side includes the hidden system prompt + assistant function result tokens in the final billed total and may attribute them differently to prompt vs completion, (2) client-side estimator they run might not emulate the server's tokenization of function_call arguments or streaming fragments. Also check whether the client retried briefly which would multiply counts in billing logs.

billing: I pulled the invoice line item for req_0a9f3c — we show 52,142 tokens across their account for that day, but per-request logs show several large requests from that API key within seconds. The invoice sums all requests in the billing window; one of the large entries is an async batch that includes function responses with long payloads (weather report + logs) — those are included in total_tokens on the server.

maya: the customer insists it's a single request. they supplied a timeline that shows a web retry at 15:01:12 where the client re-sent the payload after a 5xx and then streamed the remainder. Could that produce duplicated accounting?

sre-oncall: retries can produce duplicate billing. but our metering dedupe only works for identical request_id headers if present. The SDK by default does not set Idempotency-Key, so an automatic client retry would be treated as a separate request for billing. Check request headers in metering-service logs: ``idempotency-key`` presence is key.

mayanote: here's the JS SDK snippet they used to count tokens client-side (redacted):
```js
const est = tokenizer.estimateTokens(messages);
console.log('client tokens', est);
// using tiktoken-lite 0.4.1 on browser
```

jordan: that estimator will mismatch if any server-side system messages are injected (e.g., feature flags that wrap instructions) or if function_call arguments are expanded server-side. Also streaming can add partial chunks that the server counts when appended to the completion but the client might not include in their local final text estimate.

billing: action: I ran a raw meter query for req_0a9f3c and the surrounding 60s. Results: three requests: req_0a9f3c (116 tokens), req_0a9f3c-retry (115 tokens), and batch_job_8891 (51,911 tokens) which was a separate background job triggered by the same API key earlier that day. The invoice number 52,142 is dominated by batch_job_8891. Looks like customer's interpretation conflated the batch job with the single chat request.

maya: ok that's helpful — customer believed only interactive UI calls count. they didn't realize server-side batch ingestion under same key would bill. i'll send a writeup explaining the batch job is the main cause and show per-request lines.

jordan: to help the customer reconcile and avoid future surprises:
- recommend using separate API keys for batch jobs vs interactive clients
- encourage idempotency-key header for safe retries
- offer a small script they can run to reproduce server-side tokenization exactly: use our /v1/telemetry/tokenize endpoint (internal) or provide a server-side tiktoken binary we use

sre-oncall: also open: ENG-INFR ticket to surface a customer-friendly metering view that groups batch jobs separately in billing UI. filing now.

support-bot: created incident INC-2026-342 for tenant reconciliation, assigned to billing and eng-infra. :white_check_mark:

maria (customer): @maya thanks, please share the per-request logs. i'll ask my infra team to separate batch jobs and add idempotency keys.

maya: will follow up with logs and a short guide. assigning to billing for the invoice adjustment review and to eng-infra for metering UX improvement. Thanks all.
